item.title: Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo found guilty of murdering Dr Leli Darling
item.description: Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo has been found guilty of murdering Nadi based Doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya, who was also known as Leighley Leli Darling, with the sentencing on 4th September. Rokoralovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife at the deceased's residence in Fatima Court, Martintar, Nadi between 31st August and 1st September last year .
item.content:encoded:
Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo has been found guilty of murdering Nadi based Doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya, who was also known as Leighley Leli Darling, with the sentencing on 4th September.

Rokoralovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife at the deceased's residence in Fatima Court, Martintar, Nadi between 31st August and 1st September last year .

During the trial, it was heard that Rokoralovo and Dr Biumaitotoya were involved in a complex personal relationship marked by financial dependence, jealousy, alcohol abuse and escalating conflict, culminating in a fatal attack at the deceased's home.

The prosecution said following an argument, Rokoralovo repeatedly attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife, causing fatal injuries, before leaving the scene in the deceased's vehicle.

item.content:encoded:
The U.S citizen, Edward Zimbardi accused of running an alleged Ponzi scheme worth more than US$165 million, who was deported from Fiji to the United States to face federal charges, was living in a luxury island home here, and the question now arises on whether he had established local connections here.

The U.SÂ Embassy in Fiji confirm Zimbardi was deported on Friday following cooperation between Fijiâ€™s Ministry of Immigration, the Fiji Police Force and U.S. authorities.

FBI Supervisory Special Agent Aaron Sears who had come to Fiji says Zimbardi thought he could run off to a far-off Pacific island to avoid the FBI and live off the money he allegedly stole from his investors.

S ears says Zimbardi's life of luxury has come to an end and he now sits in a jail cell in the United States awaiting his day in court.

He adds what the FBI agents found in Fiji were upset leaders who did not want him in their country after they had found out what he is accused of doing back in the United States.

Several of the victims that the FBI had spoken to in this investigation had told them that Zimbardi told them that he had lost his money in the collapse of the program just like they did.

Special Agent Sears said vinaka to the Fijian Ministry of Immigration for the invaluable help that they provided in this investigation.

It was said that in an effort to avoid the reach of law enforcement, Zimbardi travelled internationally for years.

Last June, before criminal charges had been filed, the FBI encountered Zimbardi at the Atlanta-Hartsfield-Jackson Airport.Â

He told the agents that he had plans to fly to Fiji for a month, and Zimbardi took that trip but almost immediately after he arrived, he cancelled his return ticket to the United States.

U.SÂ Attorney for the Northern District of Georgia, Theodore S. Hertzberg says the FBI agents travelled to Fiji and in an undercover capacity escorted Zimbardi back to the United States and immediately arrested him upon touching down at LAX in California.

Zimbardi faces federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering in connection with the alleged scheme, which reportedly victimised thousands of people.

Hertzberg says Zimbardi allegedly tricked thousands of people into investing in his â€œCrypto Program” by promising huge returns.

He says Zimbardi allegedly used the money for risky currency trades, payments to early investors, a house and expensive vehicles instead.

Zimbardi faces wire fraud and money laundering charges.

fijivillage News has sent further questions to the U.S authorities. We are awaiting their response.

item.title: 17-year-old questioned over alleged temple theft in Howell Road
item.description: A 17 year old boy is being questioned in relation to an alleged case of sacrilege whereby money was stolen from a temple in Howell Road yesterday morning. Police say the matter was reported yesterday morning.
item.content:encoded:
A 17 year old boy is being questioned in relation to an alleged case of sacrilege whereby money was stolen from a temple in Howell Road yesterday morning.

Police say the matter was reported yesterday morning.

A temple committee member told fijivillage News that $2,000 was stolen among other items.

We have also received information that the juvenile was also involved in another temple break in in Nasinu two weeks ago, we are following up with Police regarding this.

The juvenile is currently in custody at the Samabula Police Station as investigations continue.

item.title: Seruiratu disappointed as Sugar Minister absent during important industry discussions
item.description: Leader of the Opposition Inia Seruiratu says he is disappointed that Minister for Sugar Charan Jeath Singh was not present in Parliament during discussions on important issues affecting the sugar industry. Seruiratu raised the concern during debate on the Standing Committee on Economic Affairs' Review Report on the Sugar Cane Growers Council Annual Report 2022.
item.content:encoded:
Leader of the Opposition Inia Seruiratu says he is disappointed that Minister for Sugar Charan Jeath Singh was not present in Parliament during discussions on important issues affecting the sugar industry.

Seruiratu raised the concern during debate on the Standing Committee on Economic Affairs' Review Report on the Sugar Cane Growers Council Annual Report 2022.

He says Singh was only served a yellow card for one and a half hours and also did not attend any of the meetings of the Special Committee on Sugar.

Seruiratu says they are discussing serious issues affecting the sugar industry and need people who are serious about the sector.

Parliament Speaker Filimone Jitoko says he will leave it to Singh to explain his absence.

The Opposition Leader further says let's support our farmers, without the farmers, there will be no FSC, s o let's provide all the support that's needed to keep the industry going.

Seruiratu says he hopes that the Government will take the lead, particularly from the Office of the Minister, because it's serious and they really need all the efforts from both sides of the House .

Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica says the Sugar Cane Growers Council plays an important role in looking after the welfare of cane farmers.

Kamikamica says one issue identified by the Special Committee during its consultations was the need for adequate farmer representation on the Council.

He says urgent attention needs to be given to the issue and hopes it can be addressed before the end of the financial year, either through elections or the nomination of farmer representatives.

Kamikamica also supports recommendations for timely financial reporting, better demographic data on farmers and improved financial transparency within the Council.

He says there needs to be a clearer breakdown of financial information so people can better understand how Government grant funding provided to the Council is being used.

Kamikamica also supports the introduction of key performance indicators for the Council and says proper farmer representation should be addressed as soon as possible.

item.title: Government reviews 26 iTaukei laws as Opposition raises concerns about uncertainty
item.description: Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga says its review of laws affecting iTaukei land, resources and traditional institutions is aimed at strengthening rights and correcting past concerns, while Opposition MP Jone Usamate says any changes must be based on truth and goodwill and should clearly benefit iTaukei people. While delivering his ministerial statement, Turaga says 26 laws introduced between
item.content:encoded:
Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga says its review of laws affecting iTaukei land, resources and traditional institutions is aimed at strengthening rights and correcting past concerns, while Opposition MP Jone Usamate says any changes must be based on truth and goodwill and should clearly benefit iTaukei people.

While delivering his ministerial statement, Turaga says 26 laws introduced between 2007 and 2022 had been identified for review, with nine already repealed, amended or superseded.

Turaga says the Government's approach is anchored in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and that reforms must be undertaken through consultation and within Fiji's constitutional and legal framework.

While responding in the iTaukei language, Usamate says Opposition MPs are ready to assist with the review but questioned the need for changes that could create fear or uncertainty among iTaukei communities.

He says no iTaukei land was sold between 2007 and 2022 and highlighted developments during the period, including improved access to electricity and water, bridge construction and changes to the administration of iTaukei land and lease money.

Usamate is urging the Government to ensure any changes to existing laws preserve measures that have benefited iTaukei people.

He also welcomed the re-establishment of the Great Council of Chiefs but called on the Government not to politicise chiefs and traditional leaders.

Turaga then says Government will not trade one injustice for another and that reforms must address legitimate grievances without creating new legal uncertainty for landowners, families and communities.

He says the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Bill 2025 is before the Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights, while work is also progressing on the Traditional Knowledge and Cultural Expressions Bill.

Turaga adds that the Constitutional Reform Commission had completed its nationwide consultations and is finalising its report for submission to the President on the 31st of this month.
